        {
          role: [32m'tool'[39m,
          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'BGj4aVkUhsG8bayr'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,
              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'Title: \n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'URL Source: https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview.md\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Markdown Content:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://wasp.sh/llms.txt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'---\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Overview\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Auth is an essential piece of any serious application. That's why Wasp provides authentication and authorization support out of the box.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's a 1-minute tour of how full-stack auth works in Wasp:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Embedded content](https://www.youtube.com/embed/Qiro77q-ulI?si=y8Rejsbjb1HJC6FA)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Enabling auth for your app is optional and can be done by configuring the `auth` field of your `app` spec:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  name: "MyApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  wasp: { version: "^0.24" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  title: "My app",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`  head: ["<link rel='icon' href='/favicon.ico' />"],\n`[39m +
                      [32m'  auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    methods: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      usernameAndPassword: {}, // use this or email, not both\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      email: {}, // use this or usernameAndPassword, not both\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      google: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      gitHub: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/someRoute",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about the `auth` field options in the [API Reference](#api-reference) section.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We will provide a quick overview of auth in Wasp and link to more detailed documentation for each auth method.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Available auth methods\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp supports the following auth methods:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Email »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Email verification, password reset, etc.](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Username & Password »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[The simplest way to get started](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Google »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/google)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Users sign in with their Google account](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/google)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Github »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/github)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Users sign in with their Github account](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/github)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Keycloak »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/keycloak)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Users sign in with their Keycloak account](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/keycloak)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Slack »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/slack)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Users sign in with their Slack account](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/slack)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Discord »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/discord)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Users sign in with their Discord account](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/discord)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Click on each auth method for more details.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's say we enabled the [Username & password](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass) authentication.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We get an auth backend with signup and login endpoints. We also get the `user` object in our [Operations](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/operations/overview) and we can decide what to do based on whether the user is logged in or not.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We would also get the [Auth UI](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/ui) generated for us. We can set up our login and signup pages where our users can **create their account** and **login**. We can then protect certain pages by setting `authRequired: true` for them. This will make sure that only logged-in users can access them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We will also have access to the `user` object in our frontend code, so we can show different UI to logged-in and logged-out users. For example, we can show the user's name in the header alongside a **logout button** or a login button if the user is not logged in.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Different ways to use auth\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you have decided which auth methods you want to support, you can also choose how you want to present the authorization flows to your users.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Generated components\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This is the fastest way to ship, with Wasp generating ready-made components for your app. They allow for some customization to make them consistent with your app. You don't need to implement any UI or logic, and they just work.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Email »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Username and password »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Social Auth »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/overview)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Make your own UI {#custom-auth-ui}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp is flexible enough to let you completely customize your login and signup interface. We give you the auth related functions, and you decide how and when to call them. This allows for total customization of the look-and-feel, and the interaction, but it needs a bit more work.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Email »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email/create-your-own-ui)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Username and password »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass/create-your-own-ui)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [Social Auth »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/create-your-own-ui)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::tip\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You don't have to choose one *or* the other! Mix-and-match, and use what you need in each moment. For example, you can create a custom signup screen, but use Wasp's generated components for login.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Custom login and signup actions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The previously discussed options should cover the vast majority of cases. But, for the few instances where it is not enough, you can [create your own signup flows](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/advanced/custom-auth-actions), with completely custom logic. This is not recommended, and reserved for advanced use cases. Please check first if other Wasp features (mainly [auth hooks](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/auth-hooks)) can handle your requirements.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Protecting a page with `authRequired`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When declaring a page, you can set the `authRequired` property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you set it to `true`, only authenticated users can access the page. Unauthenticated users are redirected to a route defined by the `auth.onAuthFailedRedirectTo` field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import Main from "./src/pages/Main" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("MainRoute", "/", page(Main, { authRequired: true })),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::caution[Requires auth method]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can only use `authRequired` if your app uses one of the [available auth methods](#available-auth-methods).\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If `authRequired` is set to `true`, the page's React component (passed as the first argument to `page(...)`) receives the `user` object as a prop. Read more about the `user` object in the [Accessing the logged-in user section](#accessing-the-logged-in-user).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Logout action\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We provide an action for logging out the user. Here's how you can use it:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/components/LogoutButton.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { logout } from "wasp/client/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const LogoutButton = () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return <button onClick={logout}>Logout</button>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Accessing the logged-in user\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can get access to the `user` object both on the server and on the client. The `user` object contains the logged-in user's data.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `user` object has all the fields that you defined in your `User` entity. In addition to that, it will also contain all the auth-related fields that Wasp stores. This includes things like the `username` or the email verification status. For example, if you have a user that signed up using an email and password, the `user` object might look like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const user = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // User data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: "cluqsex9500017cn7i2hwsg17",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  address: "Some address",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Auth methods specific data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    email: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      id: "user@app.com",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      isEmailVerified: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      emailVerificationSentAt: "2024-04-08T10:06:02.204Z",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      passwordResetSentAt: null,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can read more about how the `User` is connected to the rest of the auth system and how you can access the user data in the [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities) section of the docs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### On the client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are two ways to access the `user` object on the client:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- the `user` prop\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- the `useAuth` hook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Getting the `user` in authenticated routes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If the page's spec sets `authRequired` to `true`, the page's React component receives the `user` object as a prop. This is the simplest way to access the user inside an authenticated page:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import Account from "./src/pages/Account" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("AccountRoute", "/account", page(Account, {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      authRequired: true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    })),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/pages/Account.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { AuthUser } from "wasp/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import Button from "./Button";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { logout } from "wasp/client/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const AccountPage = ({ user }: { user: AuthUser }) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <Button onClick={logout}>Logout</Button>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      {JSON.stringify(user, null, 2)}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  );\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default AccountPage;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Getting the `user` in non-authenticated routes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp provides a React hook you can use in the client components - `useAuth`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This hook is a thin wrapper over Wasp's `useQuery` hook and returns data in the same format.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/pages/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { useAuth, logout } from "wasp/client/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { Link } from "react-router";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import Todo from "../Todo";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export function Main() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const { data: user } = useAuth();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  if (!user) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        Please <Link to="/login">login</Link> or{" "}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <Link to="/signup">sign up</Link>.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      </span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    );\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  } else {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <button onClick={logout}>Logout</button>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <Todo />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      </>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    );\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### On the server\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Using the `context.user` object\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"When authentication is enabled, all [queries and actions](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/data-model/operations/overview) have access to the `user` object through the `context` argument. `context.user` contains all User entity's fields and the auth identities connected to the user. We strip out the `hashedPassword` field from the identities for security reasons.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/actions.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { Task } from "wasp/entities";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { CreateTask } from "wasp/server/operations";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { HttpError } from "wasp/server";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type CreateTaskPayload = Pick<Task, "description">;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'expor'[39m... 15588 more characters
                  }
                ]
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          role: [32m'assistant'[39m,
          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-call'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'tq5E1hHoxOkeTmdv'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,
              input: {
                url: [32m'https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities.md'[39m
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          role: [32m'tool'[39m,
          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'tq5E1hHoxOkeTmdv'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,
              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'Title: \n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'URL Source: https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities.md\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Markdown Content:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://wasp.sh/llms.txt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'---\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Accessing User Data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"First, we'll check out the most practical info: **how to access the user's data in your app**.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Then, we'll dive into the details of the **auth entities** that Wasp creates behind the scenes to store the user's data. For auth each method, Wasp needs to store different information about the user. For example, username for [Username & password](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass) auth, email verification status for [Email](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email) auth, and so on.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll also show you how you can use these entities to create a custom signup action.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Accessing the Auth Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you receive the `user` object [on the client or the server](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#accessing-the-logged-in-user), it will contain all the user fields you defined in the `User` entity in the `schema.prisma` file. In addition to that, it will also contain all the auth-related fields that Wasp stores. This includes things like the `username` or the email verification status. In Wasp, this data is called the `AuthUser` object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### `AuthUser` Object Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All the `User` fields you defined will be present at the top level of the `AuthUser` object. The auth-related fields will be on the `identities` object. For each auth method you enable, there will be a separate data object in the `identities` object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `AuthUser` object will change depending on which auth method you have enabled in the Wasp file. For example, if you enabled the email auth and Google auth, it would look something like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**User Signed Up with Google**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the user has only the Google identity, the `AuthUser` object will look like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const user = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // User data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: "cluqs9qyh00007cn73apj4hp7",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  address: "Some address",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Auth methods specific data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    email: null,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    google: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      id: "1117XXXX1301972049448",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**User Signed Up with Email**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the user has only the email identity, the `AuthUser` object will look like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const user = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // User data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: "cluqsex9500017cn7i2hwsg17",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  address: "Some address",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Auth methods specific data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    email: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      id: "user@app.com",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      isEmailVerified: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      emailVerificationSentAt: "2024-04-08T10:06:02.204Z",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      passwordResetSentAt: null,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    google: null,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the examples above, you can see the `identities` object contains the `email` and `google` objects. The `email` object contains the email-related data and the `google` object contains the Google-related data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Make sure to check if the data exists]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Before accessing some auth method's data, you'll need to check if that data exists for the user and then access it:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (user.identities.google !== null) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const userId = user.identities.google.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You need to do this because if a user didn't sign up with some auth method, the data for that auth method will be `null`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's look at the data for each of the available auth methods:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Username & password](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const usernameIdentity = user.identities.username\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Username that the user used to sign up, e.g. "fluffyllama"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  usernameIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Email](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const emailIdentity = user.identities.email\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Email address the user used to sign up, e.g. "fluffyllama@app.com".\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // `true` if the user has verified their email address.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.isEmailVerified\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Datetime when the email verification email was sent.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.emailVerificationSentAt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Datetime when the last password reset email was sent.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  emailIdentity.passwordResetSentAt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Google](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/google) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const googleIdentity = user.identities.google\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Google User ID for example "123456789012345678901"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  googleIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [GitHub](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/github) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const githubIdentity = user.identities.github\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // GitHub User ID for example "12345678"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  githubIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Keycloak](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/keycloak) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const keycloakIdentity = user.identities.keycloak\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Keycloak User ID for example "12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  keycloakIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- [Discord](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/social-auth/discord) data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const discordIdentity = user.identities.discord\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Discord User ID for example "80351110224678912"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  discordIdentity.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you support multiple auth methods, you'll need to find which identity exists for the user and then access its data:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (user.identities.email !== null) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const email = user.identities.email.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (user.identities.google !== null) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const googleId = user.identities.google.id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### `getFirstProviderUserId` Helper\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `getFirstProviderUserId` method returns the first user ID that it finds for the user. For example if the user has signed up with email, it will return the email. If the user has signed up with Google, it will return the Google ID.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be useful if you support multiple authentication methods and you need *any* ID that identifies the user in your app.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type AuthUser } from "wasp/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const MainPage = ({ user }: { user: AuthUser }) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const userId = user.getFirstProviderUserId()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/tasks.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const createTask: CreateTask<...>  = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const userId = context.user.getFirstProviderUserId()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\\* Multiple identities per user will be possible in the future and then the `getFirstProviderUserId` method will return the ID of the first identity that it finds without any guarantees about which one it will be.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Including the User with Other Entities\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Sometimes, you might want to include the user's data when fetching other entities. For example, you might want to include the user's data with the tasks they have created.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll mention the `auth` and the `identities` relations which we will explain in more detail later in the [Entities Explained](#entities-explained) section.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::caution[Be careful about sensitive data]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You'll need to include the `auth` and the `identities` relations to get the full auth data about the user. However, you should keep in mind that the `providerData` field in the `identities` can contain sensitive data like the user's hashed password (in case of email or username auth), so you will likely want to exclude it if you are returning those values to the client.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can include the full user's data with other entities using the `include` option in the Prisma queries:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/tasks.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const getAllTasks = (async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return context.entities.Task.findMany({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    orderBy: { id: "desc" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    select: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      id: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      title: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      user: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        include: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            include: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              identities: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                // Including only the `providerName` and `providerUserId` fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                select: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                  providerName: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                  providerUserId: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}) satisfies tasks.GetAllQuery<{}, {}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you have some **piece of the auth data that you want to access frequently** (for example the `username`), it's best to store it at the top level of the `User` entity.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For example, save the `username` or `email` as a property on the `User` and you'll be able to access it without including the `auth` and `identities` fields. We show an example in the [Defining Extra Fields on the User Entity](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#1-defining-extra-fields) section of the docs.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Getting Auth Data from the User Object\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you have the `user` object with the `auth` and `identities` fields, it can be a bit tedious to obtain the auth data (like username or Google ID) from it:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function MainPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div className="tasks">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      {tasks.map((task) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <div key={task.id} className="task">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          {task.title} by {task.user.auth?.identities[0].providerUserId}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp offers a few helper methods to access the user's auth data when you retrieve the `user` like this. They are `getUsername`, `getEmail` and `getFirstProviderUserId`. They can be used both on the client and the server.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### `getUsername`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It accepts the `user` object and if the user signed up with the [Username & password](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass) auth method, it returns the username or `null` otherwise. The `user` object needs to have the `auth` and the `identities` relations included.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getUsername } from "wasp/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function MainPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div className="tasks">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      {tasks.map((task) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <div key={task.id} className="task">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          {task.title} by {getUsername(task.user)}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### `getEmail`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It accepts the `user` object and if the user signed up with the [Email](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/email) auth method, it returns the email or `null` otherwise. The `user` object needs to have the `auth` and the `identities` relations included.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/MainPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getEmail } from "wasp/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function MainPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div className="tasks">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      {tasks.map((task) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <div key={task.id} className="task">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          {task.title} by {getEmail(task.user)}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``'[39m... 10257 more characters
                  }
                ]
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        },

              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'Title: Overview | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Markdown Content:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp supports username & password authentication out of the box with login and signup flows. It provides you with the server-side implementation and the UI components for the client side.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Setting Up Username & Password Authentication[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass#setting-up-username--password-authentication "Direct link to Setting Up Username & Password Authentication")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To set up username authentication we need to:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1.   Enable username authentication in the Wasp file\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2.   Add the `User` entity\n'[39m +

                      [32m'4.   Use Auth UI components in our pages\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"import { SignupPage } from "./src/pages/auth" with { type: "ref" }// Configuring e-mail authenticationexport default app({  name: "myApp",  wasp: { version: "^0.24" },  title: "My App",  head: ["<link rel=\'icon\' href=\'/favicon.ico\' />"],  auth: {    // ...  },  spec: [    // Defining routes and pages    route("SignupRoute", "/signup", page(SignupPage)),    // ...  ],})`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1. Enable Username Authentication[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass#1-enable-username-authentication "Direct link to 1. Enable Username Authentication")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's start with adding the following to our `main.wasp.ts` file:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"export default app({  name: "myApp",  wasp: { version: "^0.24" },  title: "My App",  head: ["<link rel=\'icon\' href=\'/favicon.ico\' />"],  auth: {    // 1. Specify the user entity (we\'ll define it next)    userEntity: "User",    methods: {      // 2. Enable username authentication      usernameAndPassword: {},    },    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login"  },  // ...})`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about the `usernameAndPassword` auth method options in the [`UsernameAndPasswordConfig` API Reference](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/UsernameAndPasswordConfig).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2. Add the User Entity[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass#2-add-the-user-entity "Direct link to 2. Add the User Entity")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `User` entity can be as simple as including only the `id` field:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   JavaScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   TypeScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema.prisma\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`// 3. Define the user entitymodel User {  id Int @id @default(autoincrement())  // Add your own fields below  // ...}`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can read more about how the `User` is connected to the rest of the auth system and how you can access the user data in the [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities) section of the docs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 3. Add the Routes and Pages[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass#3-add-the-routes-and-pages "Direct link to 3. Add the Routes and Pages")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next, we need to define the routes and pages for the authentication pages.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Add the following to the `main.wasp.ts` file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
